BUCKETS are PROMPTS.md's two: environment (the box has not run setup) and
defect (the probe cannot start for its own reasons). All eighteen cleared rows
were defect, which is not what their messages looked like: ten ended in the path
of a missing llama-server, which reads as environment. It was not. Each of those
ten had NO ARGUMENT PARSER, so `--help` was not answered, it was RUN, and the
missing binary was only where the run stopped first. That is the reading that
makes this a safety fix and not tidying: on a box where setup.sh has put a real
llama-server in bin/, those ten `--help` runs reach the loader. Under this
checker MEASURED_INFERENCE_DRY_RUN stops them at gpu_lock's fence. A person
typing `--help` at a shell has nothing stopping them at all.
'A help request must never start work' is the standing rule; see the comment in
scripts/quant-ladder/three-file-12gb-fit.py, which overwrote its own result file
under a smoke test before it grew a --help test.

was: Sixteen scripts had no argument parser, so `--help` was not answered, it was
RUN. Where each one stopped: ten at the missing llama-server, two at a missing
results/<slug>/machine.json, two on a KeyError from looking '--help' up in a
subcommand dict, one on FileNotFoundError from opening '--help' as a
result-JSON path, and one on its three required positional arguments.
fix: An EARLY GUARD, before any work and before any dispatch:
if "--help" in sys.argv[1:] or "-h" in sys.argv[1:]:
print(USAGE.rstrip())
return
with a module-level USAGE naming what the script measures, its positional
arguments in order, the environment variables it reads, one worked example,
whether it takes the card, and the file it writes.
The CLI is UNCHANGED and deliberately so. These are invoked positionally by
stage files, by campaign work scripts and by each other, so restructuring them
into argparse would break callers that cannot be seen from here. The guard adds
an answer to --help; it takes nothing away.
The pattern is the one scripts/quant-ladder/three-file-12gb-fit.py already
carried, and probe-smoke-test.py's answers_help() recognises it, so these
sixteen have also left the checker's 'no --help test' list.
